name: Starcounter
tagline: In-memory .NET application platform where C# classes are database tables, with no ORM in between.
description: Starcounter, built in Stockholm since 2006, combines an ACID in-memory database with a .NET application runtime in what it calls a VMDBMS: database objects live in the same memory as application objects, so C# classes are tables, you query them with SQL, and there is no ORM or network hop. Durability comes from transaction logs written to disk. Version 2.0 (2013) bundled a web framework with server-side view models synced to the browser by JSON patches; 3.0 (release candidate December 2019, launched 2020) moved to .NET Core with a cross-platform CLI and Windows failover clustering. The company now markets an AI-oriented enterprise software platform built on the same engine, and public documentation still centres on 3.0.

pricing.notes: Licensing is arranged with the vendor.

scale.notes: Single in-memory node sized to RAM; 3.0 supports Windows Failover Cluster for HA.

strengths: No ORM: C# classes are persisted directly as database tables
Application code and data share memory, removing network round-trips
ACID transactions with disk logging for durability
Runs on .NET Core on Windows and Linux in 3.0
weaknesses: Tied to .NET; other languages cannot use it directly
Proprietary, with limited public information on current releases
Dataset must fit in RAM on a single node
Small ecosystem outside its Swedish customer base
useCases: Line-of-business .NET applications needing very fast transactions
Retail and supply-chain systems with heavy in-memory workloads
